assumptions.text: IdealMac at each delivery: a tag verifies only if it was minted for exactly that claim, in every state.
assumptions.real_world: No real signature or MAC scheme with a total verifier meets it in every state (U478; Attack.TotalVerifierBreaksIdealMac; TotalReading.NoIdealMac).

assumptions.text: A2_MintOnlyOnCheck: every mint of one of our ids signs CheckedClaim(pre, t) for some pre, t with Authorizes(pre, t).
assumptions.real_world: The issuer (ts/refund-finality/minter.ts) signs only after the compiled RefundFinality.Check returns true. minter.ts is TESTED only.

assumptions.text: A5: the sink's sigOk boolean equals the model's VerifyTag on the delivered token at each delivery.
assumptions.real_world: sink.ts calls Ed25519 verify on exactly the bytes that the model calls the claim. Decomposed (RepairedBytes) into H3b, H3c, B5, H3d-B6 and the trace-local A4-NOCOLL-RUN; H3a is retired.
assumptions.superseded_for: the hash core (B5 on BytesOf); kept for the value-core and V3-core edges

assumptions.text: H1_SignatureAuthenticity (claim level, step-local): a delivered token whose tag verifies carries a claim signed earlier.
assumptions.real_world: Ed25519 EUF-CMA AND secrecy of the signing key; holds up to a negligible forgery probability, only while the key is secret.

assumptions.text: H1B_ByteUnforgeability: byte string and tag that verify were signed earlier (symbolic EUF-CMA at byte level).
assumptions.real_world: Same as H1, stated on bytes; with H3b/H3c/B5/H3d-B6/A4-NOCOLL-RUN it gives H1 and A5 (RepairedBytes.RepairedGiveClaimAuthenticity). [f3] The hash core uses it DIRECTLY on BytesOf(token) (SliceSafetyBytesV3.H1B_ByteUnforgeability), with no H3 glue.

assumptions.text: H3a: the claim serialization is injective (on model claims that carry the full pre-state).
assumptions.real_world: FALSE for the real token: the token carries only SHA-256 of the pre-state, so two pre-states with one hash give one byte string (ByteAttacks.PreStateCollisionBreaksApprovedSpec; ByteAttacks.HashedPreSerNotInjective). RETIRED.
assumptions.retired_reason: False for the real token (hash of the pre-state only).

assumptions.text: H3b: at each delivery the sink rebuilds exactly Ser(ClaimOf(tok)) from the parsed token.
assumptions.real_world: sink.ts rebuilds the signed bytes; not proved.
assumptions.superseded_for: the hash core (BytesOf by definition); kept for the value-core edges

assumptions.text: H3c: the model VerifyTag is the byte verifier applied to Ser(claim).
assumptions.real_world: A definition choice of the model; no real-world content beyond H3a and B5.
assumptions.superseded_for: the hash core (no uninterpreted VerifyTag); kept for the value-core edges

assumptions.text: B5 / B5_VerifierBoolean: at each delivery the sink boolean sigOk is the byte verifier on the signed bytes of the delivered token (value core: the rebuilt bytes; hash core: BytesOf(token)).
assumptions.real_world: Node OpenSSL Ed25519 verify returns the mathematical verifier value; glue sink.ts:71-75 (sink.ts:74 signedBytes(token.body)). [f3] reworded for the hash core.

assumptions.text: Every trace lemma (L0 to L3, several charges) starts from the EMPTY store; a restart from a non-empty store is covered only as one trace from the empty store.
assumptions.real_world: A deployed sink restarts on an existing database. [f3] A restart theorem now exists for the V3 MODEL (T-RESTART, T-AUDIT; DRAFT) under NO-ROLLBACK and AUTHENTIC-INIT; the layered lemmas themselves still start empty. Scope limit, not a fact about the world.

assumptions.text: BETA-VALUES: Dafny int and HOL int are both the mathematical integers; Dafny bool and HOL bool agree; a Dafny string whose chars are < 256 and the HOL string with the same code list denote the same value.
assumptions.real_world: ARGUED, not proved (two tools, no common semantics): b-export-bridge/BRIDGE_STATEMENT.md section 2; Orchestrator A FIELDS_FOR_B.md.

assumptions.text: BETA-OPS: each of the nine export forms (Eq on bool/int/string, Neq, And, Or, Imp, Le, Not) and three literal forms has the same reading in Dafny (as written by gen_exported.py) and in the HOL Dafny semantics.
assumptions.real_world: ARGUED by a table of source line references (BRIDGE_STATEMENT.md section 2); gen_exported.py is an unproved reader cross-checked by a second reader (Mirror.dfy trees equal).

assumptions.text: BETA-ORDER: the export names bind the same argument and tuple positions on both sides (charge, request, original, remaining, enabled, opened, candidate, amount, reason).
assumptions.real_world: ARGUED: a charge/request swap on BOTH sides is invisible to both proofs (contract symmetric); a one-sided swap fails (A: NB1 go exit 1). BRIDGE_STATEMENT.md section 3.

assumptions.text: A6x_ArtifactMeetsExportedContractOnBytes: the artifact flat function meets the three exported clauses on byte-string inputs.
assumptions.real_world: A hypothesis in Dafny; equivalent to A6b (A6xIffA6b). Real-world reading needs A7-ART and the HOL chain X1 to X10.

assumptions.text: A7-ART: the artifact function of the Dafny lemma is the HOL function refund_fields, and the run-time bytes are the UTF-8 encodings of its string fields.
assumptions.real_world: Names one function on two sides; no tool relates them (U539). The executable computes refund_fields only through X1 to X10 (open).

assumptions.text: OS process contract of the launcher: the OS delivers the complete stdout of a terminated child, reports a signal or exit status truthfully, and enforces the launcher timeout.
assumptions.real_world: macOS process and pipe semantics; trusted. CE-1 and CE-2 (exit 0 with truncated or empty stdout) show why exit status alone is not success.

assumptions.text: Pinned Node 24.3.0 with its OpenSSL and built-in SQLite runs sink.ts, minter.ts and the compiled core as written.
assumptions.real_world: Trusted runtime.

assumptions.text: NO-ROLLBACK: the durable store is never rolled back to an earlier state (for example an honest prefix of its own ledger).
assumptions.real_world: Review r-restart (HIGH): a rollback to an honest prefix passes AuditFull and AuditFullSpec, and the dropped token commits again (AttackRestart.RollbackPassesAuditAndReplays). NO audit over the database alone can detect it. Needs an external monotonic anchor; none exists.

assumptions.text: AUTHENTIC-INIT: the initial charge state that the restart audit replays from is the authentic charge record.
assumptions.real_world: Review r-restart (HIGH): the audit init is an unauthenticated input; a forged init passes the spec audit (AttackRestart.ForgedInitPassesSpecAudit). AuditSpecMoney bounds money only RELATIVE to the supplied init.

assumptions.text: NO-DELETE-RECREATE: a charge store is never deleted and then created again with the same charge id.
assumptions.real_world: Review r-restart (MEDIUM): delete + re-create defeats the key invariant and gives a double refund (AttackRestart.DeleteRecreateDoubleRefund). KeyedStore has no Delete action.

assumptions.text: CREATE-AUTHORITY: every charge store is created only through the checked Create (key == init.chargeId, key absent, 0 <= remaining <= original).
assumptions.real_world: Proved as an invariant for the MODEL (KeyedStore.KExecWellKeyed). sink.ts and the dispatcher do not enforce it: the TypeScript chargeKey check is opt-in and sits in an UNAPPLIED diff (b-restart sink-keyed-chargeid, 556b55fb...; r-restart MEDIUM).

assumptions.text: A2p_MintsAreIssued: every mint of bytes with the pinned spec and checker ids signs bytes that IssueBytes produced from an authorized transition (IssuedFrom); the signing key is only in the issuer.
assumptions.real_world: Needs an issuer that signs ONLY the output of the proved IssueTokenBytes (draft minter_issuebytes.ts, d-minter; TESTED 581 requests) and key isolation. The deployed minter.ts builds the body in TypeScript (not IssueTokenBytes).

assumptions.text: A4_HashBindsInRun (trace-local, ONE hypothesis): at each delivery, the hash of the STORED charge equals the hash of an earlier mint pre-state only if the two states are equal.
assumptions.real_world: SHA-256 collision resistance on the pairs of one run. Covers both the signature binding (old A4-NOCOLL-RUN) and the sink hash compare (old A4b) for the hash-comparing core (SliceSafetyBytesV3).

assumptions.text: SERMODEL-MIRRORS-ENCODING: SerModel (SerBody, SignedBytes, ParseExact, WfBody) computes what ts/refund-finality/encoding.ts computes (canon, signedBytes, isTokenBody).
assumptions.real_world: TESTED only: b-ser 443/443 bodies; r-ser 6,581 bodies + 4,736 malformed texts, 0 differences (r-ser/conf/result.2.json). Lone surrogates: separate run. Not proved.

assumptions.text: DECODER-TYPES (type-level decoder glue): the sink decoder gives token fields of the model types (money fields as naturals, ids as hex texts); this replaces B6 for the hash core.
assumptions.real_world: The hash core needs no decoder fact beyond the types (SliceSafetyBytesV3 header). The real decoder (encoding.ts isTokenBody) is not proved to give those types; TESTED with SERMODEL-MIRRORS-ENCODING.

assumptions.text: G-H: the issuer shell passes preHashHex == lowercase hex SHA-256 of canon(pre) for the SAME pre that it passes to IssueTokenBytes.
assumptions.real_world: Named glue assumption of IssueBytes2.dfy (d-minter); the method cannot check it. A wrong hash with a reachable colliding state breaks the slice theorem.
